annotations.description:
[PROD] `GET /v1/users` returned unexpected error responses, or no status at all, in the last 10 minutes (status ≥ 400 excluding 400/401/403/404/409/498, or null).

<http://grafana:3000/explore?schemaVersion=1&panes=%7B%22a%22%3A%7B%22datasource%22%3A%22grafanacloud-logs%22%2C%22queries%22%3A%5B%7B%22refId%22%3A%22A%22%2C%22datasource%22%3A%7B%22uid%22%3A%22grafanacloud-logs%22%7D%2C%22expr%22%3A%22%7Bservice_name%3D%5C%22gp-api%5C%22%2C%20deployment_environment_name%3D%5C%22prod%5C%22%7D%20%7C%3D%20%5C%22GET%20%2Fv1%2Fusers%5C%22%20%7C%20json%20%7C%20request_endpoint%20%3D%20%5C%22GET%20%2Fv1%2Fusers%5C%22%20%7C%20exception_type%20%21%3D%20%5C%22%5C%22%22%7D%5D%2C%22range%22%3A%7B%22from%22%3A%22now-1h%22%2C%22to%22%3A%22now%22%7D%7D%7D|Open this route's error lines> to read the exception each failing request logged (type, message, stack trace) before deciding what to fix. *View in Grafana* shows only the count that fired.

A **null** status means gp-api never wrote one: the request was killed in flight, usually by the gateway’s ~120s idle timeout. Only those running longer than 30 seconds are counted — a shorter one is the caller hanging up, which is not a fault and is far more common. Check `responseTimeMs` on those lines; a cluster at ~120,000ms is the timeout, not the handler.
